result.topic_en: The page states two transformation formulas for series involving the divisor function sigma_s(n), the Riemann zeta function and tan(pi s/2): one relating a gamma-weighted series in (x ± iλ) to a series with exponentially damped sines, and one symmetric in α and β with αβ = 4π², built from the series Σ σ_s(n) sin(nα).
result.transcription:
(77)
Add MS a 94 (18(77))

$\sigma_s(n)$ is the sum of the $s^{th}$ powers of the divisors of $n$.

$\Gamma(s+\frac{1}{2})\left\{\frac{\zeta(1-s)}{(s-\frac{1}{2})x^{s-\frac{1}{2}}} + \frac{\zeta(-s)\tan\frac{1}{2}\pi s}{2x^{s+\frac{1}{2}}} + \sum_{\lambda=1}^{\lambda=\infty}\frac{\sigma_s(\lambda)}{2i}\left[(x-i\lambda)^{-s-\frac{1}{2}}-(x+i\lambda)^{-s-\frac{1}{2}}\right]\right\}$

$=(2\pi)^s\left\{\frac{\zeta(1-s)}{2\sqrt{\pi x}} - 2\pi\sqrt{\pi x}\,\zeta(-s)\tan\frac{1}{2}\pi s + \sqrt{\pi}\sum_{\lambda=1}^{\lambda=\infty}\frac{\sigma_s(\lambda)}{\sqrt{\lambda}}e^{-2\pi\sqrt{2\lambda x}}[?]\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+2\pi\sqrt{2\lambda x}[?]\right)\right\}$

If $\alpha\beta=4\pi^2$, then

$\alpha^{\frac{s+1}{2}}\left\{\frac{1}{\alpha}\zeta(1-s)+\frac{1}{2}\zeta(-s)\tan\frac{1}{2}\pi s+\sigma_s(1)\sin\alpha+\sigma_s(2)\sin 2\alpha+\cdots\right\}$

$=\beta^{\frac{s+1}{2}}\left\{\frac{1}{\beta}\zeta(1-s)+\frac{1}{2}\zeta(-s)\tan\frac{1}{2}\pi s+\sigma_s(1)\sin\beta+\sigma_s(2)\sin 2\beta+\cdots\right\}$

methods.what: Transformation formula for a gamma-weighted divisor series in (x ± iλ) into a series of exponentially damped sines, involving zeta(1-s), zeta(-s) and tan(πs/2)
Modular-type transformation for the series Σ σ_s(n) sin(nα), symmetric in α and β with αβ = 4π²

items.english: The gamma-weighted divisor series equals (2π)^s times the stated expression with exponentially damped sine terms.
If αβ = 4π², then the α-expression involving Σ σ_s(n) sin(nα) equals the corresponding β-expression.
